Available Length: Following the hype and high expectations from the first single's music video, Rocky then released another single later on July 21st, 2011 titled “Peso”, another hit under Rocky’s belt, just before the mixtape was intended to release. From here, the mixtape was then delayed to August for unknown reasons. While this release date also did not go as planned Rocky 'leaked' a song from the mixtape, an early version of "Trilla" on September 17th, 2011. The excitement by fans for the upcoming project was through the roof, Drake even saw how big Rocky was getting and invited him to be a part of him and Kendrick Lamar’s Club Paradise tour. In early October Rocky signed a recolutionary two-year $3 million dollar record deal. Finally after all the waiting, on Halloween 2011 the project “LIVE.LOVE.A$AP” was officially released. This mixtape is widely known for its slowed down, Houstan influanced, psychedelic and dream-like sounds which made it stand out from many other hip-hop projects from this time period and it would become a gigantic pioneer for the genre of cloud-rap for many years to come. Much later in 2021 the tenth anniversary of the mixtape released which was missing certain songs such as "Kissin' Pink" "Out Of This World" and "Purple Swag: Chapter 2" along with different versions of the songs "Leaf" and "Acid Drip", but featured a new song inspired by the original project titled “Sandman” dedicated to the late A$AP Yams who evidently had a ton of influence on the project with production by someone who had plenty of production on the original mixtape, Clams Casino along with a newer collaborator Kelvin Krash.

Available Length: With Rocky on the rise with massive success from his mixtape “LIVE.LOVE.A$AP” it only made sense for the A$AP Mob to all make a project together so more of the other members of A$AP could be recognized for their talents, and they did just that. The project was first announced by Rocky in a November 29th, 2011 interview with HipHopDX with him stating “Yeah, “LONG.LIVE.A$AP.” That’s like the joint with everybody on it. It’s a compilation. I plan on dropping that after “LIVE.LOVE.A$AP” drops again, because we gonna do a deluxe version of “LIVE.LOVE.A$AP”. Right after that, we gonna drop the A$AP compilation with everybody on it.” The project has been described as a compilation at the time and the title would later become the name of Rocky’s first studio album. The project was said for a February 2012 release which was eventually pushed back for an April release but by the time March came around a May release was revealed. This was revealed in a Tumblr post from the A$AP Mob speaking on the release of A$AP Ant and Bodega Bamz song “Told Ya” on March 26th, 2012 states “The baby goon of the year A$AP Ant brings you his first visual alongside Bodega Bamz produced by DJ Carnage. Look out for TRILLUMINVTI this May featuring new music from Pretty Flacko, Nasty Baby 90’s Nigga, Twelvy the Good Goon, Fergenstein aka Diamond Dolla$ Page, and the rest of the Mob”. In this post a new name for the project can be seen “Trilluminati” and again, was set to be released in May 2012. A fan asked where the project was in April and Yams responded on his Tumblr on May 2nd, 2012  saying that the A$AP Mob thought moving to LA “would be the move”, but it ended up being the total opposite. He claimed “The energy is dead here there was no motivation here to make music”. He then said they’re going back to New York City to get the inspiration they needed again, Yams stated “the music will be rawer than ever believe that....TRILLUMINATI will be here” again confirming the title. With the project still not coming out in May many still wondered if it would be released any time soon, finally in July Yams announced the first single for the album “Bath Salt” which was released on July 27th. Yams stated there were no more delays and the album would come out on August 28th officially announcing the title “Lord$ Never Worry”. Before this another single “Purple Kisses” released on August 13th and the last single “Work” released on August 20th. Finally, after all the delays “Lord$ Never Worry” released on the planned date of August 28th, 2012.

Available Length: After the massive success of Rocky’s first mixtape and a revolutionary three million dollar record deal he decided to go full force into his first studio album seemingly right away. While still being a part of the Club Paradise Tour with Drake and Kendrick Lamar he began to make connections with bigger names in the industry. Not too long after the release of the hit mixtape Rocky talked about compilation album with the A$AP Mob then titled "LONG.LIVE.A$AP". Still working on his own album by March 2012 Rocky's album name was rumored to be "A$AP Rocky Forever Part 1" which was quickly debunked and was now titled "LONG.LIVE.A$AP" with the A$AP Mob's project being renamed to "Trilluminati". At this point the album was planned to drop on July 4th, 2012, but the album would later be delayed. Fans were hungry for more solo Rocky music as he had been featuring on a handful of songs up until April 16th, 2012 when the first single for his album "Goldie" released with production from a very well respected producer Hit-Boy. The album was delayed once the July release day hit for unknown reasons, but Rocky still worked on the album with a second single titled "Fuckin' Problems" releasing on October 24th, 2012. This song has the likes of Drake, Kendrick Lamar and 2 Chainz and quickly became Rocky's most popular song at that point, and remains as one of them to this day. It was then announced in December 2012 that the album would release on January 15th, 2013 with the title track "Long Live A$AP" releasing as a single on December 18th, 2012. Just two days later on December 20th, 2012 a listening event for the album took place at a local Harlem music store. The album was completely finished and ready to release on its planned day, this was when just two days after that on December 22nd, 2012 the whole album was leaked online for everyone to hear. Surprisingly, Rocky was not upset by this, infact he was completely okay with it as long as people liked the album as he spent so much time making it. Just four days before the album the last pre-release single titled "Wild for the Night" with Skrillex and Birdy Nam Nam, which was also a huge hit. The album then released on the planned date of January 15th, 2013 along with a deluxe edition adding four more songs to the tracklist. The album is credited for its creative direction as well as big time features after being for the most part unknown not too long before the release. Despite this, Rocky knew the songs such as "Fuckin' Problems" and "Wild for the Night" were made as hits for his record label in a sense and knew he wanted to create a more personal and creative album next.

Available Length: It was revealed in a 2019 interview with Kerwin Frost that Rocky was taught how to make beats in 2011 by close collaborators at the time A$AP Ty Beats and SpaceGhostPurrp, so on his first studio album that was titled  "LONG.LIVE.A$AP" he had a number of production credits. Some songs that he had a large amount of production on is "Suddenly" and "Jodye" which he produced with the likes of Héctor Delgado and Joey Fatts. After the release of that studio album Rocky had a plan to being working on a mixtape full of self-produced instrumentals. This mixtape would not be announced until a interview with WiLD 94.9 on April 12th, 2013 where he said "I'm working on an instrumental album right now. I'm doing all my own beats," he says. "It's going to be interesting to see how people react towards my production." Rocky said he's "not even going to announce it, just drop it" very soon. Although fans would not see a release of the mixtape anytime in 2013 Rocky continued to work on it while touring with the likes of Héctor Delgado, who evidently had a lot of influence on the project. Then later on Rocky would speak on the project in a interview with MTV saying "I think people are gonna be intrigued by it because it's actually good," he continued. "I wouldn't do nothing that I didn't feel confident or comfortable about. I think people gonna like this shit". He revealed the title to be "Beauty and the Beast: Slowed Down Sessions, Chapter 1" and described the mixtape as "really druggy, ambient shit", following up saying "everything is like classical beautiful music and boom-bap Wu-Tang shit mixed together. It's slowed down and it's real vibey, with no lyrics. I feel like it's gonna get people through the summer" stating it would release for free that summer of 2013 with visuals. These three SoundCloud singles all had the same cover art with the new title of “DUMMIE” with a which would have likely been the final album art. It has been stated by Mod that the album was intended to drop with “TESTING” on May 25th, 2018, but the whole album was entirely scrapped just a few weeks before for unknown reasons.
